name: VPN Egress
tagline: VPN subscription endpoints in your provider’s exit rotation
description: Adds subscription endpoints to the exit set of the providers you list: the gateway fetches each subscription, parses it, probes every endpoint, keeps the best ones and drops the ones that stopped answering. Where those endpoints sit is up to you — rotated together with the provider’s own source addresses (default), held back as the fallback tier, or preferred on their own. Selection scope, count, quality threshold and refresh interval are all configurable per provider list. This extension ships only its own runtime and UI addons — no gateway code is required for it to work.
author: aurora

ui.help: List the providers or pools this applies to as a comma-separated list (* for every provider). Then pick where their endpoints sit: rotated with the provider’s own source addresses, held back as the fallback tier, or preferred on their own.

fields.label: Applies to
fields.description: Comma-separated provider or pool names. * applies to every provider. A trailing * matches by prefix (zen-*).

fields.label: Exit rotation
fields.description: rotate: these endpoints and the provider's own source addresses form one rotation. fallback: they take over once the source addresses fail or are rate-limited. vpn_only: they are preferred and the source addresses are the last resort.

fields.label: Subscriptions
fields.description: One entry per line (or comma-separated): a subscription URL, a node URI pasted as-is, or a bare token when a subscription base URL is set. Plain URI lists and base64-encoded payloads are both accepted.

fields.label: Subscription headers
fields.description: Optional JSON object of HTTP headers sent when fetching subscriptions, for example {"Authorization":"Bearer …"}.

fields.label: Subscription base URL
fields.description: Optional. A bare token on the Subscriptions line is appended to this URL, so the list can hold only the token. Leave empty when every entry is already a full URL or a node URI.

fields.label: Refresh interval (minutes)
fields.description: How often subscriptions are re-fetched and endpoints re-probed. 0 disables scheduled refresh.

fields.label: Endpoints to keep
fields.description: How many endpoints to keep after sorting. 0 keeps all of them.

fields.label: Selection order
fields.description: Sort the probed endpoints by latency: best first, worst first, or shuffled.

fields.label: Quality threshold (ms)
fields.description: Endpoints slower than this are dropped. 0 keeps every endpoint that answers.

fields.label: Probe samples
fields.description: Number of connection attempts per endpoint; the median is used.

fields.label: Probe timeout (ms)
fields.description: Per-sample connection timeout. Endpoints that never answer are removed.

fields.label: Protocols
fields.description: Comma-separated protocols to keep, for example vless,vmess,ss,trojan.

fields.label: Regions to keep
fields.description: Comma-separated region/name fragments to keep. Empty keeps everything.

fields.label: Local SOCKS ports
fields.description: Comma-separated local ports your tunnel core listens on. One port = one exit; several ports let the gateway rotate between them.

fields.label: Tunnel core
fields.description: none: report endpoints only, no local ports expected. static: you run the core and map each local port to an endpoint yourself. singbox: the gateway switches the active endpoint through the core's Clash API.

fields.label: Core HTTP API
fields.description: Base URL of the core's control API, for example http://127.0.0.1:9090.

fields.label: Core API secret
fields.description: Optional bearer token for the core's control API.

fields.label: Core selector group
fields.description: Proxy group or outbound tag the endpoint is switched on.

items: Exit rotation decides where these endpoints sit: alongside the provider's own source addresses (rotate), behind them (fallback) or in front of them (vpn_only).
Each attempt picks one exit, and a failed attempt moves to the next one instead of repeating the same failure.
A rate limit demotes the tier it was reported on, so the next tier takes over until the window ends.
An endpoint that stops answering is cooled down automatically and returns once it recovers.
Endpoints are probed, sorted by latency, filtered by the quality threshold and trimmed to the configured count.
Endpoints that do not answer within the probe timeout are removed rather than kept as dead weight.
Subscriptions are re-fetched on the configured refresh interval.

blocks.text: Review every subscription and endpoint you add. This extension contacts third-party services you configure.

banners.message: VPN egress contacts the subscription endpoints you configure. Review them before enabling.

requirements: A tunnel core listening on the local ports listed in the extension settings, unless core_kind is none
Local source addresses configured on each provider (bind_ips) if you want them mixed into or preferred over the endpoints
notes: This extension only contributes exits; it does not change how the gateway talks to providers.
Subscription URLs, headers and the core API secret are stored in the gateway's extension config.
Review third-party extensions before installing them from a store.
